lines: Lots of computers sit switched on, doing nothing, for most of the day.
Their owners could rent them out, even for a few minutes, and earn some money.
But letting a stranger use your computer is hard, and it feels risky.
You would have to give them a key, and that key keeps working until you remember to take it back.
Or you would have to trust a company in the middle, and install its software.
And AI assistants can now pay for things, but sign-up forms are made for people.
Sublet solves this. It lets anyone rent out a computer by the minute.
It works like a hotel key card. It opens one room, and it stops working at checkout.
The renter pays only for the minutes they need, and nobody gets a key that lasts forever.
And an AI assistant can rent a computer too, all by itself.
Here's how it works.
First, the owner changes one setting on their computer. There's nothing to install.
Then they put it up for rent, with a price per minute.
A renter chooses how many minutes they want, and pays.
The payment is checked, and the renter gets a key card for that one computer, for exactly that time.
They log in and use it, just like normal.
When the time is up, the key card stops working, and they are logged out automatically.
And the money goes to the owner.
So who checks the payment and hands out the key cards? Not a company, and not one person.
It's done by NEAR, a public network run by many computers around the world.
The rules are written where anyone can read them, and nobody can change them.
Even the master key that makes the key cards is split into pieces, so no one can make one on their own.
We tried it for real, on a test computer. We paid for two minutes.
The key card arrived in about ten seconds, and we were in.
Two minutes later, we were logged out, right on time, and the same key card no longer worked.
That's Sublet. Rent out a computer by the minute, with no company in the middle.
It's a hackathon project, running on NEAR's test network.
